definitions.explanation: Things that cause worry or distress. Refers to personal matters that weigh on one's mind, such as relationship issues, work problems, or health concerns.

examples.english: I have something on my mind.

examples.japanese: {悩|なや}み{事|ごと}があったら{相談|そうだん}してね。
examples.english: If you have any worries, talk to me about it.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}、{仕事|しごと}の{悩|なや}み{事|ごと}が{多|おお}くて、なかなか{眠|ねむ}れない。
examples.english: Lately, I have so many work-related worries that I can't sleep well.

notes:
USAGE:
A very common everyday word. The suffix ～{事|ごと} turns a noun or verb stem into a compound meaning "matters related to ~." {悩|なや}み{事|ごと} is more specific and concrete than {悩|なや}み alone, implying particular issues or problems rather than a general state of worry.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {悩|なや}み{事|ごと}がある (to have worries)
- {悩|なや}み{事|ごと}を{相談|そうだん}する (to consult about one's worries)
- {悩|なや}み{事|ごと}を{抱|かか}える (to carry worries)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悩|なや}み: worry, distress — the general state of being troubled
- {心配事|しんぱいごと}: things to worry about — focuses more on anxiety about future outcomes
